scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Formation dancing began in 1932 at London's Astoria Ballroom, introduced by Olive Ripman as "pattern dancing." It became a competitive sport in England during the 1930s and expanded internationally.
The dance form was featured on BBC's Come Dancing program in the 1960s and has grown globally since.
on_screen: Map: United Kingdom (origin) · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Formation dance is performed in competitions governed by the International DanceSport Federation and national bodies.
It is a sport emphasizing teamwork, synchronization, and technical skill.
The dance is also performed for exhibitions and television programs.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Wild Turkey Trio (https://archive.org/details/wild-turkey-trio_202102)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Teams of 6 to 8 couples dance choreographed routines lasting up to six minutes, including walk-on and walk-off sections.
Couples perform synchronized steps to the beat, forming patterns such as diamonds, circles, and lines.
Latin formation includes Cha Cha, Rumba, Jive, Paso Doble, and Samba, while Standard formation includes Waltz, Quickstep, Tango, Viennese Waltz, and Foxtrot.
Watch for Chain Reaction, Roundabout, Velberter Rose.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music for formation dance is arranged to fit the choreography, typically lasting six minutes with entrance, main, and exit parts separated by a gong.
The main part, which is judged, lasts 3 to 4.5 minutes.
The pulse is Varies by dance; Latin dances often in 4/4, Waltz in 3/4 at about 120 beats a minute.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Men in Standard formation wear black or midnight blue tailcoats; in Latin formation, men wear uniform colored shirts, often black.
Women may wear varied dresses within competition rules.
The dance floor is used fully to display patterns, with clear visibility of formations prioritized.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Olive Ripman introduced formation dancing in 1932.
Specialist choreographers include Ona Skaistutė Idzelevičienė, Roberto Albanese, Horst Beer, and Rachael Holland.
Formation dancing is practiced internationally with notable competitions in England, Germany, and Austria.
Formation dance evolved from ballroom dancing and pattern dancing introduced in early 20th-century England.

Formation dance is shares music of Latin dancesport: Formation Latin routines use the five International Latin dances.

steps_as_taught.name: Arm scoop and step back
steps_as_taught.description: Scoop right arm across body, step out on right leg and push left hand underneath.

steps_as_taught.name: Swings and punch
steps_as_taught.description: Swing right arm and step back, then punch with right arm.

steps_as_taught.name: Pottys and body roll
steps_as_taught.description: Do pottypaws / grapevine footwork combined with body rolls and chest pops.

steps_as_taught.name: Jump and punch
steps_as_taught.description: Two jumps with arms punching to the left corner.

steps_as_taught.name: Step and elbow
steps_as_taught.description: Step out with the left leg and elbow with the right arm, then step with the right and elbow with the left.

steps_as_taught.name: Circle arms
steps_as_taught.description: Circle arms all the way around and bring them into an elbow shape.

steps_as_taught.name: Twist
steps_as_taught.description: Twist out to the left with hands flat in front of the face.
